# std::geometry::frame

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/std-geometry-frame.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

The properties of the ordered frames of smooth affine objects, from ADR 0001 §11. A frame b of a smooth affine object X of dimension n has n columns in the coordinate frame of X, which form the matrix P(p) at each point p. The module declares the families `Frame<X>`, `Coords<b>`, `CoCoords<b>` and `FrameMap<b, c>`. The application declares each frame and each frame primitive, which names its frames. The frame array of a vector v at p in b is P(p)⁻¹v, and the frame array of a covector α at p is P(p)ᵀα. The transition from b to b′ at p is P_b′(p)⁻¹·P_b(p). The failure value ⊥ lies over no point.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/std-geometry-frame.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/std-geometry-frame.toml).

<a id="frame.static-identity"></a>

## Frames are static

- Property: `frame.static-identity`
- Subject: `std::geometry::frame::Coords`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §11, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-1)

An array or a map array names its frames in its type. A frame primitive accepts an operand only in the frame that its binding or its other operands require: decoding in the frame of its binding, `frame_apply` with the source frame of the map, `frame_coapply` with the target frame of the map, `frame_compose` with equal middle frames, and `frame_pairing` and `frame_equal` in one frame. Any other operand is an error (`E_ENDPOINT`).

- Example: Let b = columns((1, 0), (1, 2)) and b2 = columns((2, 0), (0, 1)) be frames of the plane. Comparing the array of a vector in b with its array in b2 is an error (`E_ENDPOINT`) that names `Coords<b>` and `Coords<b2>`.
- Run by: `arrays_in_different_frames_of_one_object_are_rejected_statically` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

Claims:

- `binding`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FramePrimitives.lean): `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameDecode_association`, `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameApply_association`, `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameCoapply_association`, `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameCompose_association`, `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.framePairing_association`, `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameEqual_association`
  - Premises: none
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: Each theorem characterizes the operand types that the shape of a frame binding associates with a result: the frames of the operands must be equal where the statement requires it. The kernel's typing of a call reads that association, so the theorems concern checked bindings and the Rust frontend relates them to source declarations.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `arrays_in_different_frames_of_one_object_are_rejected_statically` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - `a_frame_of_an_object_outside_cinf_affine_is_rejected` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
  - Note: The first test compares arrays in two frames of one object. The second declares a frame of an object that is not a smooth affine object, which the kernel rejects (`E_FRAME`).

<a id="frame.embedded"></a>

## Primitives embed their declared frames

- Property: `frame.embedded`
- Subject: `std::geometry::frame::Frame`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §11, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-1)

A valid frame primitive embeds each frame that it names exactly as that frame is declared: its object, its matrix P and its inverse Q. A binding with another object, matrix or inverse is not valid.

- Example: The primitive `enc_b = frame_encode(Tangent, Coords, frame = b)` carries the columns (1, 0) and (1, 2) of b and the inverse that the kernel computes for them.
- Run by: `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

Claims:

- `binding`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FramePrimitives.lean): `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameDeclared_spec`, `VastitasOracle.FramePrimitives.frameDeclared_object`
  - Premises:
    - the embedded frame passes `frameDeclared`, which the kernel's contract of every frame binding requires
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

<a id="frame.adequacy"></a>

## Decoding after encoding

- Property: `frame.adequacy`
- Subject: `std::geometry::frame::Coords`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §11, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws-1)

Decoding the frame array of a vector or a covector in a frame b gives back the vector or covector, and encoding a decoded array gives back the array. The failure value ⊥ stays ⊥.

- Example: At p = (1, 2) the vector (3, 2) has the array (2, 1) in b = columns((1, 0), (1, 2)), and the array decodes to (3, 2). The covector (2, 1) has the array (2, 4) in b, which decodes to (2, 1).
- Run by: `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameRuntime.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime.adequacy`
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance.c4_adequacy`
  - Premises:
    - for `adequacy`: P(p)·Q(p) = Q(p)·P(p) = I at every point p, which `VastitasOracle.FrameDeclarations.frame_sound` proves for every frame declaration of a valid environment
    - for `c4_adequacy`: the declaration environment of the module is valid, the operand of the inner call evaluates to a value of its checked type, and `frame_encode(frame_decode(a))` encodes in the frame that it decodes from
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: `adequacy` states the four identities of the frame runtime: decoding undoes encoding and encoding undoes decoding, for vectors and for covectors. A fiber without one point coordinate and one component per frame vector gives the failure value, and the failure value stays the failure value. `c4_adequacy` states the same of accepted Core: the type `Coords<b>` fixes the frame in which `frame_decode(frame_encode(v))` decodes, and the valid environment makes the embedded frame invertible.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - `mutated_frame_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.FrameRuntimeRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/FrameRuntimeRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
    - [`VastitasKernel.FrameRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/FrameRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
- `native`: [Not claimed](../specifications.md#not-claimed)
  - Reason: The frame runtime is Lean code that the checker and the generated programs share. No claim states that the compiled native code refines it. Tests run the native code.

<a id="frame.transitions"></a>

## Transitions

- Property: `frame.transitions`
- Subject: `std::geometry::frame::FrameMap`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §11, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws-1)

For frames b and b′ of one object, the transition from b to b′ at a point p takes the array of a vector in b to its array in b′. The transitions from b to b′ and from b′ to b at p are inverse to each other.

- Example: Let r = columns((1, 0), (x, 1)), with the inverse columns((1, 0), (-x, 1)). At p = (1, 2) the transition from r to b takes the array (1, 2) in r to the array (2, 1) in b, and the transition back gives (1, 2) again.
- Run by: `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameRuntime.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime.transition_laws`
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance.c5_transitions`
  - Premises:
    - for `transition_laws`: the point has n coordinates, P_b(p)·Q_b(p) = Q_b(p)·P_b(p) = I and P_b′(p)·Q_b′(p) = Q_b′(p)·P_b′(p) = I at the point, and the vector has n components
    - for `c5_transitions`: the declaration environment of the module is valid, and the point operand evaluates to a value of its checked type
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: `transition_laws` states that the transition from b to b is the identity, that the transition from b′ to b″ after the transition from b to b′ is the transition from b to b″, that the transitions from b to b′ and from b′ to b are inverse, and that a transition sends the array of a vector in b to its array in b′. `c5_transitions` states the first three laws of accepted Core, and that no transition between frames of two objects is accepted.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - `frame_program_checks_builds_and_prints_42` in [`tests/frame_primitives.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/frame_primitives.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.FrameRuntimeRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/FrameRuntimeRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
    - [`VastitasKernel.FrameRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/FrameRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)

<a id="frame.change-of-frame"></a>

## Change of frame of a map array

- Property: `frame.change-of-frame`
- Subject: `std::geometry::frame::FrameMap`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §11, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws-1)

Let F be a smooth map, p a point, b and b′ frames of its source and c a frame of its target. The map array of F at p in (b′, c) is the map array in (b, c) after the transition from b′ to b at p.

- Example: For f(x, y) = x² + y at (1, 2) and the frame l = columns((2)) of the line, the map array in (b, l) is (1, 2). After the transition from r to b it is the map array (1, 3/2) in (r, l).
- Run by: `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameRuntime.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime.frameMatrix_natural`
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance.c7_two_frame_pairs`
  - Premises:
    - for `frameMatrix_natural`: F is well typed from n to m coordinates, the point has n coordinates, the frames b and c are invertible at p and at F(p), and the inverses of b′ and c′ have n and m rows
    - for `c7_two_frame_pairs`: the declaration environment of the module is valid, and the map and point operands evaluate to values of their checked types
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: Both theorems state the law for two pairs of frames, (b, c) and (b′, c′): the map array in (b′, c′) is the transition from c to c′ at F(p), after the map array in (b, c), after the transition from b′ to b at p. When c′ is c the first transition is the identity (`transition_laws`). The proofs read the rows of a map array as the Jacobian through `VastitasOracle.SmoothCalculus.backward_eq_cot`, a chain-rule theorem of the oracle.
- `bridge`: [Proved (bridge)](../specifications.md#proved-bridge)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasBridge.Differential.Frame`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-bridge/VastitasBridge/Differential/Frame.lean): `VastitasBridge.Differential.frame_arrays_same_map`
    - [`VastitasBridge.Differential.AcceptedFrames`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-bridge/VastitasBridge/Differential/AcceptedFrames.lean): `VastitasBridge.Differential.checked_frame_arrays_same_map`
  - Premises:
    - for `frame_arrays_same_map`: F is well typed from n to m coordinates, the point has n coordinates, and the four frames are invertible at p or at F(p)
    - for `checked_frame_arrays_same_map`: the declaration environment of the module is valid, and the map and point operands evaluate to values of their checked types
  - Assumes: [mathlib](assumptions.md#assumption.mathlib), [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: The two map arrays in (b, c) and (b′, c′) decode, with `Matrix.toLin` in their frames, to one linear map: the Fréchet derivative `fderiv ℝ` of the real map of F at p. The second array is the first between the transitions `Q_c′·P_c` and `Q_b·P_b′`. The proofs read the reverse pass through `reverse_covector_eq_comp_fderiv` and use no chain-rule theorem; `lean-bridge/Audit.lean` checks this.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - `mutated_frame_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - `frame_program_checks_builds_and_prints_42` in [`tests/frame_primitives.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/frame_primitives.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.FrameRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/FrameRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)

<a id="frame.pairing"></a>

## Pairing in a frame

- Property: `frame.pairing`
- Subject: `std::geometry::frame::CoCoords`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §11, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws-1)

The pairing of the coframe array of a covector α with the frame array of a vector v in the same frame is α(v), whatever the frame.

- Example: The covector (2, 1) and the vector (3, 2) at (1, 2) pair to 8. Their arrays (2, 4) and (2, 1) in b pair to 8 as well.
- Run by: `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameRuntime.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameRuntime.pairing_invariant`
    - [`VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/FrameAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.FrameAcceptance.c6_pairing`
  - Premises:
    - for `pairing_invariant`: P(p)·Q(p) = I at the point p of the covector, and the covector and the vector each have one point coordinate and one component per frame vector
    - for `c6_pairing`: the declaration environment of the module is valid, and the covector and vector operands evaluate to values of their checked types
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: `c6_pairing` states that an accepted `frame_pairing` of two encodings pairs arrays in one frame, which the call fixes, and evaluates to the pairing of the covector and the vector, a value that names no frame. Over two different points the pairing reads (0, 0).
- `bridge`: [Proved (bridge)](../specifications.md#proved-bridge)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasBridge.Differential.Frame`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-bridge/VastitasBridge/Differential/Frame.lean): `VastitasBridge.Differential.pairing_in_frame`
  - Premises:
    - the covector and the vector lie over one point, where P·Q = Q·P = I, and each has one point coordinate and one component per frame vector
  - Assumes: [mathlib](assumptions.md#assumption.mathlib)
  - Note: The pairing of the two arrays is the sum over i of the coordinate i of the covector in the dual basis times the coordinate i of the vector in the frame, as a basis of ℝⁿ, and it equals α ⬝ᵥ v.
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `frames_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_frames.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_frames.rs)
    - `frame_program_checks_builds_and_prints_42` in [`tests/frame_primitives.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/frame_primitives.rs)
